title: EU evening ops briefing — KV eviction & autoscaler follow-ups
body:
Shift: EU evening (17:00-23:00 CET)
Owner: Asha Patel (handoff author)
Summary: Short window of elevated tail latency and a ~2% increase in 5xxs across the hosted API in eu-west between 18:12–18:48 CET. Probable driver was repeated KV cache evictions coincident with aggressive node scale-down from the HPA; when new pods came up they served cold and produced increased latencies and occasional timeouts. No customer-facing outages or large-scale data loss; saw increased error budget burn on several customer routes.

Incidents observed (order of importance):
- RED-3418: "eu-west: intermittent 5xx spikes on hosted text generation" — first page at 18:14. Peak error rate 2.3% (baseline ~0.1%). 99p latency peaked at ~420ms (baseline ~95ms).
- RED-3421: "KV cache thrash — eviction storms during scale operations" — internal tracking ticket opened 18:50.
- RED-3424: minor blips in metrics pipeline ingestion for eu-west (delayed metrics ingestion ~3–6 minutes) — caused some noise in alerting.

Timeline (high-level):
- 18:12 CET: Alerts triggered for increased 5xx rate on api-hosted* routes.
- 18:14 CET: Triage: checked host-level metrics, saw correlate with pod churn on inference pool eu-west-1a.
- 18:18 CET: Reached out to infra (Lucas) via Slack for node autoscaler overview. Confirmed that HPA + cluster-autoscaler scale-down kicked in at 18:05–18:10 window.
- 18:24 CET: Applied temporary variant: pinned one pod group to min-replicas=3 for 10 minutes to stabilize.
- 18:28 CET: Error rate reduced but tail latency still elevated; found cache-miss rate increase in KV cache telemetry.
- 18:42 CET: Rolled back an experimented aggressive LRU config deployed earlier today (PR ref in linked_artifacts).
- 18:50 CET: Opened RED-3421 to track KV eviction root cause and follow-ups.
- 19:10 CET: Incident considered mitigated; monitoring continues.

Actions taken during shift (what we did):
- Stabilized the pool by temporarily increasing min-replicas for affected pods (quick mitigation).
- Rolled back the LRU tuning that increased eviction aggressiveness (PR #987).
- Tuned alerting thresholds to reduce noisy pages during metrics ingestion delay (short-term).
- Created RED-3421 to track root cause and cross-team work (infra + runtime).

Evidence & quick diagnostics:
- Grafana dashboard: "eu-west serving — latency & errors" shows spike starting 18:12 and recovery by 19:00.
- KV cache telemetry: cold-start miss rate jumped x14 during churn window; memory pressure on pods concurrently increased.
- Cluster autoscaler logs: several nodes marked for termination at ~18:06 and drained rapidly, causing pod reschedules.

Unresolved items & follow-ups (with owners):
- RED-3421 (Samir): Deep-dive to separate whether eviction pattern is due to LRU behavior or OS-level OOM reclaims on quantized models. Deliverable: root-cause writeup by 2026-03-21.
- RED-3422 (Lucas): Validate cluster-autoscaler cooldown configuration for eu-west autoscaling group. Proposed change: increase scale-down grace to 10m (current 2m). Target due 2026-03-20.
- Runbook update (Asha): Add a short playbook for "KV eviction storm" with checklist items (pin pool, rollback cache tuning, increase metrics retention window). Draft by 2026-03-19.
- Monitoring (Morgan): Instrument a dedicated "KV cold-start miss rate" alert that triggers before 5xx threshold; propose threshold and run it in test for 48 hours. Owner to post proposal in RED-3425.

Runbook/Playbook notes (draft ideas to include):
- Immediate mitigation checklist: 1) Pin min-replicas for affected pool; 2) Rollback recent cache tuning PRs; 3) Disable rapid scale-down for pool; 4) Watch 99p latency and cache miss rate for 15 min.
- Diagnostic commands / dashboards to check (short commands): kubectl get pods -n inference -l pool=eu-west -o wide 
  kubectl top pod <pod> 
  curl -sS http://prometheus/api/v1/query?query=kv_cache_miss_rate
- Escalation criteria: error rate > 1% for >10 min OR 99p latency > 300ms for >10 min -> page platform on-call (pagerduty).

Post-shift recommendations to next shift:
- Monitor RED-3421 and the autoscaler RFC in RED-3422. If root cause points at LRU config, schedule a slow canary (10% traffic) with reduced eviction pressure.
- Keep min-replicas pinned for the affected pool until autoscaler cooldown is increased; annotate changes carefully and link to tickets.
- Watch for related regressions: new PRs touching cache sizing or GC in runtime repo — ask reviewers to include perf benchmarks.

Notes to self / informal thoughts:
- The pattern looked exactly like cold-start churn -> cache misses -> increased tail latency. But memory pressure was also present; could be multi-factor.
- Need to validate whether memory pressure came from an unrelated regression in allocator, or if eviction policy was simply too tight for real traffic variance.
- Consider adding a synthetic warmup traffic generator in eu-west that runs during scale events so new pods warm caches before receiving live traffic. Worth prototyping.

Customer impact:
- No major customer-visible outage; a handful of sustained 5xxs for small fraction of requests (per-customer impact below SLA thresholds). CS notified proactively for top affected accounts (internal ticket CUSTOMER-1183).

Communications & next steps:
- I'll draft a short post-incident note for the weekly SRE sync once we have root-cause (target: 2026-03-22).
- Lucas to coordinate autoscaler cooldown change; Morgan to propose alert changes; Samir to lead root-cause analysis.

Attachments / quick links:
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/euwest-serving
- RED-3418 (incident): https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RED-3418
- RED-3421 (follow-up): https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RED-3421
- PR reverted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/987

If you take the shift: priorities = 1) watch RED-3421, 2) ensure pinned min-replicas remains until autoscaler change lands, 3) validate new alert proposal from Morgan, 4) poke infra if any more node-terminations coincide with latency spikes.

Sign-off: Asha (on-call) — ping me in Slack (asha.patel) if any of the follow-ups start moving and I can re-prioritize tomorrow morning.

-- end of notes --
